annotation.title_clean: Criminal Liability for Crimes Committed by Artificial Intelligence Devices (Robots)
annotation.title_en: Criminal Liability for Crimes Committed by Artificial Intelligence Devices (Robots)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Al-Haddad, R.R.A.R.; Mustafa, J.J.; Ali, M.F.
annotation.summary_en: Legal article examining whether robots can bear criminal liability for harm they cause. It reviews robot definitions, legal personality, and the elements of crime (conduct, result, causation), concluding that responsibility falls on humans such as programmers, manufacturers and users, and urges legislative intervention.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots lack awareness and will, so traditional criminal liability is difficult to apply to them directly.
Causation analysis uses equivalence and adequate-cause theories to attribute liability to programmers or users.
Surgical robot error and child injury examples illustrate robot crimes.
Calls for legislative intervention to regulate robots and determine criminal responsibility.
Discusses whether electronic legal personality should be granted to robots.
